name: Chung Eui-sun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2010-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Chung Eui-sun is the only son of Hyundai Motor Co. Chairman Chung Mong-koo and his heir apparent.
As president of Kia from 2005 to 2009, Chung grew the subsidiary auto brand faster than Hyundai Motor.
More than 40% of his fortune is derived from auto parts maker Hyundai Glovis.
In 2009, Chung became vice chairman of Hyundai Motor. He was appointed to the company's board in 2010.
forbes_facts: Chung worked at the New York office of Japanese trading house Itochu Corp. before joining Hyundai's auto parts affiliate, Hyundai Mobis, in 1994.
He is president of Asian Archery Association, as his father once was.

name: G. M. Rao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2015)
forbes_bio: Airports tycoon G.M.Rao controls India-listed airports operator GMR Airports (formerly known as GMR Airports Infrastructure.)

The company operates airports at Hyderabad and Delhi as well as the Kualanamu International Airport in Indonesia. It also provides services to the Mactan-Cebu International Airport in the Philippines.
In 2022, he hived off the non-airports business into GMR Power and Urban Infra.
Rao has a 50% stake in Indian Premier League cricket team Delhi Capitals.
The GMR Group opened the GMR School of Aviation in Hyderabad in partnership with European aircraft maker Airbus in  2024.
forbes_facts: Former jute trader, Rao split from family and moved into banking, later infrastructure.

name: Vincent McMahon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025)
forbes_bio: Vince McMahon grew World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) from a regional operation into a global phenomenon.
A third-generation wrestling promoter, McMahon grew up in a trailer park in North Carolina and joined his father's small wrestling company in 1972.
He purchased the business 10 years later and turned it into a giant. He took WWE (then named WWF) public in 1999.
In 2023, McMahon agreed to merge WWE with UFC to form TKO Group Holdings.
He stepped down as executive chairman of TKO in 2024 amid sexual misconduct allegations, which he has denied.
forbes_facts: Donald Trump picked McMahon's wife, Linda, to lead the Small Business Administration during his first term and to run the Department of Education in his second term.
McMahon's daughter, Stephanie, is married to professional wrestler Paul Levesque, better known as Triple H. She resigned as WWE's chief brand officer in 2023.

name: Gang Ye
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2021); Hurun China U40 (2020-2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Gang Ye cofounded online gaming and e-commerce firm, Sea, with Forrest Li and David Chen.
He's been the company's chief operating officer since 2017, following his previous role as chief technology officer.
Sea has attracted investors such as Tencent, the Norwegian sovereign wealth fund, private equity firm General Atlantic and Malaysian billionaire Robert Kuok's son Kuok Khoon Hua.
In 2023, Sea booked its first-ever annual net profit since its IPO in 2017.
Sea has rolled out digital banking services in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil.
forbes_facts: Ye previously worked at the Economic Development Board of Singapore and palm oil major Wilmar International.

name: Feng Hailiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Feng Hailiang chairs Zhejiang-based Hailiang Group, whose interests include copper smelting, real estate, education and agribusiness.
Feng started a trading company in 1985, followed by a copper products factory in 1989; the latter was the predecessor to Hailiang Group.
Feng's son Feng Luming is an executive director of Hong Kong-listed Hailiang International Holding.
Liming holds undergraduate and graduate degrees in business from the University of San Francisco.
Hailang Group donated more than $100 million of stock to the Hailiang Charitable Foundation in 2020.

name: Tang Binsen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2022-2023); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2022); Hurun China U40 (2021-2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Tang Binsen chairs Chi Forest, a Beijing-headquartered, unlisted beverage supplier valued at $15 billion in 2021.
Chi Forest was once known as Genki Forest.
Tang is the founding partner at Challenjers Capital, whose investments include online game company Moonton, acquired by ByteDance for $4 billion in 2021.

name: Gurbachan Singh Dhingra
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Gurbachan Singh Dhingra is the vice chairman emeritus of Berger Paints India, the country's second-largest paint maker by market share.
He controls the company with his brother Kuldip Singh Dhingra, also a billionaire.
In 1991 the brothers bought Berger Paints, then the country's smallest paint maker, from liquor tycoon Vijay Mallya.
Apart from India, Berger has a presence in Bangladesh, Nepal, Poland and Russia.
His son Kanwardip Singh Dhingra was appointed vice chairman in August 2024.

name: Wei Ying-Chiao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Wei Ying-Chiao and his three brothers, Ing-Chou, Yin-Chun and Yin-Heng, started Tingyi in 1991.
Tingyi is now one of the largest producers of ready-to-drink tea and bottled water in China. It is also a major supplier to the country's instant-noodle market.
The family also controls the Dicos fried-chicken chain.
The family's private company, Ting Hsin, sold its 37.17% stake in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building, to Itochu for $665 million in 2018.
forbes_facts: Wei graduated from a local high school in Changhua County, central Taiwan, but didn't go to  college.

name: Alexandra Daitch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexandra Daitch owns an estimated 3% stake in Cargill, the largest food company in the world.
She's one of four billionaire sisters who inherited stakes in the company from their father W. Duncan MacMillan, who died in 2006.
Her great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.

name: Steven Tisch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Steven Tisch is chairman and executive vice president of NFL's NY Giants. His late father Bob paid $75 million in 1991 for a 50% stake in the team.
Bob Tisch (d. 2005) cofounded Loews Corp. with his brother Laurence (d. 2003) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Today, Loews Corp., a publicly traded company, is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
Steven's mother Joan (d. 2017) was the largest individual shareholder of Loews with a 6% stake. His brother Jonathan is co-chairman.
Steven, Jonathan and sister Laurie Tisch, inherited their mother's fortune.
forbes_facts: Steven is the only known person to have won both an Academy Award and a Super Bowl ring: he won an Oscar for producing Forrest Gump, and the Giants won two Super Bowls.
Steven has been a movie producer for decades, working on hit films including Risky Business, American History X, and The Pursuit of Happyness.

name: K. Dinesh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2016); Hurun India (2015-2018)
forbes_bio: K. Dinesh is a cofounder of Indian tech giant Infosys.
Since stepping down from the company's board in 2011, he and his wife Asha have devoted themselves to philanthropy.
Ashraya Hastha Trust, their philanthropic arm, focuses on education, healthcare, animal welfare and agriculture.
They have funded a cancer center at the Narayana Health Hospital and a clinic; the latter is on their ancestral land in Mysore city.
forbes_facts: A math grad, Dinesh also has a doctorate in literature.

name: Vladislav Sviblov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2024); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Vladislav Sviblov derives his fortune from Bering Metals, which holds a portfolio of gold mining assets.
In 2020 Sviblov purchased Highland Gold Mining from fellow billionaire Roman Abramovich and his partners.
The next year his Highland Gold acquired Kamchatka Gold from another Russian billionaire, Viktor Vekselberg, and other shareholders.
In 2022 Sviblov bought the Russian assets of Canada's Kinross Gold for $340 million. The market value of these assets exceeded $1.5 billion, according to the Russian press.
Sviblov is a former executive of the PIK Group, the largest real estate developer in Russia controlled by billionaire Sergei Gordeev.
